patch_description:
The prior program uses a single SciPy differential-evolution run (`popsize=23`, `maxiter=520`) on the exact nonsmooth minimum, then attempts signed epigraph polishing from only one orientation cell. This can converge to a mediocre combinatorial cell and has relatively high evaluation cost.

This version uses a deterministic vectorized differential-evolution population (`96` candidates, `760` generations) directly in simplex coordinates. Its selection score is phase-dependent: early generations use the mean of the lowest `30` determinants with low weight to discover globally separated layouts; later generations narrow to the lowest `10` constraints and increase tail weight, encouraging active-constraint equalization before exact epigraph polishing. Several final elites are independently polished by SLSQP rather than trusting one global-search winner. Mutation changes from exploratory DE/rand/1 to best-directed updates, and feasibility is maintained by barycentric simplex projection.
